title: Buyer-side detection of hostile localhost seller failure modes with Anvil-fork EIP-3009 replay
control_condition: baseline localhost seller fully consistent with its own manifest
treatment_condition: single-field hostile mutations (amount, payTo, receipt keys) and an EVM-level replay on a pinned Anvil fork

baseline.note: in-memory dev key signed a payload; localhost seller returned a complete receipt; detector did not flag (correct)

amount_mismatch.note: challenge amount 99999 vs manifest 10000; cross-check detected

pay_to_mismatch.note: challenge payTo differs from manifest payTo; cross-check detected

receipt_missing_key.note: seller receipt dropped transaction or settledAmountUsdc; receipt-key check detected

receipt.revert_reason: FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled

replay.note: Anvil fork of Base pinned at block 54035433; dev payer funded via anvil_setBalance + anvil_setStorageAt (USDC slot 9); tx_hash is the fork-local first-settle tx reference, not a mainnet transaction; the identical replay with the same nonce reverted at EVM state level

conclusion: All four detection outcomes correct: baseline passes unchanged echo-verify criteria; amount-mismatch, payTo-mismatch, and receipt-missing-key are each detected by cross-checks; the same-nonce EIP-3009 replay reverts on the pinned Anvil fork.
pre_acknowledged_limitations: mock seller is harness code; deviations are controlled single-field mutations
Anvil fork state is synthetic; replay rejection demonstrates EVM nonce semantics, not live facilitator behavior
